post.summary:
Chat answers one user turn. The answer arrives as a stream, so that the UI
can show which tool the assistant is running while it is still working.
grpc-gateway serves this as an HTTP stream of newline-delimited JSON.

get.summary: ReadChat returns one of the caller's conversations with every turn of it.

delete.summary: DeleteChat removes one of the caller's conversations for good.

get.summary:
ListChats returns the caller's own conversations, newest first and without
their messages. A conversation holds whatever its author could read, so it
is never returned to anybody else.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many conversations to return, newest first. Zero means the default.

title.description: Title is the opening of the first question.

eventId.description: The event the conversation was opened from, when it was opened from one.

messageCount.description:
How many turns the conversation holds. Filled in listings, where the
messages themselves are not returned.

assistantChat.description: Chat is one stored conversation. In a listing its messages are left out.

delta.description: delta is a piece of the answer's text, to be appended as it arrives.

toolActivity.description: tool_activity reports that the assistant started or finished a tool.

confirmation.description:
confirmation asks the user to approve a tool that would change the
product. The answer stops there until they do.

secret.description:
secret carries a credential an approved tool produced. It is delivered
to the user and deliberately kept out of the conversation the model
sees, so that it never reaches an LLM provider.

suggestions.description: suggestions are follow-up questions to offer under the answer.

assistantChatChunk.description: ChatChunk is one piece of the answer. Exactly one field is set.

integrationId.description: Identifier of the AI integration whose model answers.

conversation.description:
The conversation so far, oldest first, ending with the user's new message.
No conversation state is kept on the server: the client sends the whole
history it wants the model to see.

eventId.description:
Optional identifier of an event the question is about. The event itself is
never taken from the client: the assistant reads it through the tools, so
that what the model sees is what the system recorded.

mode.description:
What the assistant is being asked to do: "chat" (the default), "explain"
for one runtime event, "digest" for a summary of a period, or "support"
to help the user write a support request. The mode only selects the
instructions the assistant is given; it never widens what it may do.

confirmId.description:
Approval of a tool call the assistant asked about in the previous turn,
carrying the identifier from that Confirmation. It is the only way a tool
that changes anything is ever run.

eventKind.description:
Which half of the product event_id belongs to: "runtime" (the default) or
"admission". The two are read with different tools, and an identifier alone
does not say which, so a client that opens a chat from an event page has to
say. Empty means runtime, for clients written before admission existed.

chatId.description:
Identifier of the stored conversation this turn belongs to. Empty starts a
new one, whose identifier comes back in the Done chunk.

id.description:
Identifier to send back as confirm_id to approve this exact call. It is
valid for a few minutes, once, and only for the user it was issued to.

tool.description: Name of the tool, for example create_rule.

title.description: Human readable title of the tool, as the MCP server named it.

arguments.description:
The arguments the tool would be called with, as pretty-printed JSON. They
come from the model, so the user is shown exactly what would be sent.

destructive.description: destructive is set when the call removes something rather than adds it.

assistantConfirmation.description:
Confirmation is a tool call the assistant wants to make and may not make on
its own: it would create, change or delete something in the product.

stopReason.description:
stop_reason is "end_turn" when the assistant finished on its own,
"confirmation_required" when it is waiting for the user to approve a tool
call, "max_iterations" when the agent loop ran out of steps, or "error".

error.description: error is set when stop_reason is "error".

iterations.description: iterations is how many model turns the answer took.

chatId.description:
chat_id is the stored conversation this turn was written to, so that a
client which started a new one learns where to continue it.

label.description: What the secret is, for example "API token ci-bot".

note.description: How the secret is to be handled.

assistantSecret.description:
Secret is a credential produced by an approved tool call. It is shown once:
the product stores only a hash of it.

assistantSuggestions.description:
Suggestions are follow-up questions to offer under the answer, written by the
model from the exchange it just had. They arrive once, just before Done.

name.description: Name of the tool, for example search_docs.

error.description:
error is set on a finished phase when the tool failed. The assistant
carries on: a failed tool is an answer the model has to account for.
